title: Trees & BSTs
subtitle: A tree decomposes into child subproblems; a BST adds ancestor-wide ordering that lets a search discard whole subtrees.
variables: n = nodes, h = height in nodes (empty 0, leaf 1), w = maximum level width, k = requested rank, B = serialized byte/character length, L = total materialized path output length. Trees are finite rooted binary trees with no cycles or shared children unless explicitly stated. Node identity, not equal val, identifies a vertex. Keys are mutually comparable, not NaN; numeric arithmetic/comparison costs use the fixed-word model, while Python large integers cost by bit length. Hash operations are expected O(1) on identity keys; long string key hashing/comparison costs must be added. Space includes recursion/explicit stacks and excludes output unless labeled. An unbalanced BST may have h=n; logarithmic operations require a balancing guarantee, not merely the BST property. All templates avoid depth-linear Python recursion; balanced construction recurses only O(log n). Paired traversal n counts compared positions and h their maximum active depth. The rerooting template uses an undirected unweighted tree with integer-labeled vertices, not binary Node links. BSTIterator O(1) amortized next is across a full traversal; init plus a prefix of m calls is O(h+m), and one call may cost O(h).

contrasts: Binary tree vs BST
Binary describes at most two ordered child slots; BST additionally constrains all descendant keys.
Balanced vs complete vs perfect
Balanced limits height differences (definition must be stated); complete fills levels left to right; perfect fills every level.
DFS vs BFS memory
DFS stores O(h) unfinished work; BFS stores O(w) frontier. Either can be O(n).
Height vs depth vs diameter
Height goes downward, depth goes from root, diameter is a longest undirected node-to-node path; specify node/edge units.
Identity vs equality
LCA references identify actual objects; equal values do not make separate vertices the same.
Path vs subtree
A path never forks; a subtree may contain many branches. Maximum path return state must have one arm.
BST validation vs sorted neighbors
Full inorder strict increase or ancestor bounds validates; immediate parent-child checks do not.
Mutation vs new root
Insertion/deletion may replace the root; assigning a local node variable alone does not update the caller.
Recursion vs explicit stack
Both retain O(h) state; explicit stack avoids interpreter call-depth limits.
Single-query vs preprocessed rank/LCA
Simple traversal often wins once; repeated queries can justify augmented sizes or ancestor tables.

decisionProcess: 0–30s: confirm true tree/no sharing/cycles, binary versus adjacency model, identity versus key, empty result and duplicate policy.
30–60s: ordered query -> BST pruning O(h); rank/iterator -> inorder; structural equality -> paired traversal. Balance is a separate guarantee.
60–90s: depth output/nearest leaf -> BFS; root path aggregate -> inherited DFS; subtree metric -> postorder summary.
90–120s: downward target count -> prefix frequency plus exit undo; turning optimum -> one-arm return/two-arm answer; single LCA -> parent map or verified BST split.
120–180s: reconstruct from constraints, serialize with nulls, reroot for every-root answers. State h/w/output costs; choose iterative for deep chains; dry-run empty/skew/duplicate/missing target.

templateDetails.preconditions: Returns (preorder,inorder,postorder) value lists; empty gives three empty lists. Does not mutate; compatible val/left/right nodes accepted. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Before/between/after are explicit phases.

templateDetails.preconditions: Returns (height_in_nodes, height_balanced_bool, diameter_in_edges); None -> (0,True,0). Explicit frames retain only O(h) summaries. No mutation. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Summaries retained only along active frames.

templateDetails.pattern: Ordered branch pruning; BST structural edits
templateDetails.preconditions: Strict unique-key BST precondition. search returns matching node or None; insertion mutates links, ignores duplicates and returns root. Keys mutually comparable. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: O(h) is logarithmic only with balance.

templateDetails.preconditions: Comparable non-None, non-NaN keys. Strict ordering rejects duplicate values; None root is valid. Does not mutate; None is used only as an unbounded endpoint. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Ancestor constraints apply to all descendants.

templateDetails.preconditions: Strict BST precondition and integer rank k. Returns value, raises ValueError for invalid rank (including empty tree). Does not mutate. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Next inorder value is smallest unvisited key.

templateDetails.preconditions: Strict unique-key BST; mutates links and may copy successor val into the found node. Returns possibly replaced root; missing key is a no-op. Node-object identity is not a stable identity for a key after deletion. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Right-minimum has at most one child.

templateDetails.preconditions: Returns node identity or None when either target absent. Node class must retain identity equality/hash (provided Node does); p is q is supported. No mutation. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Identity and presence are independent of equal values.

templateDetails.preconditions: Strict unique-key BST; query by comparable key values, not arbitrary node references. Returns split node, or None if either key missing; no mutation. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Both keys must exist before the split implies ancestry.

templateDetails.preconditions: Numeric values may be negative; only root-to-leaf nonempty paths count. None -> False; no mutation. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Internal prefix match is not a leaf path.

templateDetails.preconditions: Integer node values and target; counts all nonempty downward ancestor-to-descendant paths, not only root/leaf paths. None -> 0; no mutation. Deletes zero-count keys to keep O(h) map size. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Exit undo isolates sibling prefixes.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite numeric values, no NaN. Path may start/end anywhere but cannot revisit a node or fork. Returns nonempty best sum; None root -> None. No mutation. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Return one arm; complete answer may use two.

templateDetails.preconditions: Preorder JSON list with null child markers, integer payloads (bool rejected). serialize returns text; deserialize builds new nodes or raises ValueError for malformed shape/types. Empty tree is [null]. Neither mutates existing nodes. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Every token fills one child slot.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite sequences of unique hashable keys with consistent equality. Returns new tree; []/[] -> None. Invalid lengths, duplicates, mismatched keys or inconsistent orders raise ValueError. Does not mutate; O(n) slicing copy included in stated auxiliary bound. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Preorder opens ancestors and inorder closes them.

templateDetails.preconditions: Strictly increasing comparable non-NaN sequence; validates ordering. Builds fresh height-balanced nodes without slicing; empty -> None. Recursion is logarithmic, not input-tree-depth dependent. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Index ranges avoid recursive slice allocations.

templateDetails.preconditions: Mutates each existing node by swapping child links and returns same root identity (None -> None). Inversion generally destroys BST ordering; applying twice restores topology. Tree topology must be finite with no shared children or cycles.
templateDetails.observation: Swapping existing links twice restores original topology.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite binary tree, no sharing/cycles. Returns values grouped by depth; empty -> []; no mutation. Last value per row yields right view; saving only that value avoids full O(n) output.
templateDetails.observation: Snapshot is exactly one depth.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite binary trees, no sharing/cycles. Returns value-and-shape equality or mirror equality; symmetric checks one tree. Empty pair equal; one empty side unequal. No mutation; not identity equality.
templateDetails.observation: One missing child breaks shape equality.

templateDetails.preconditions: Strict BST unchanged during iteration. Yields increasing values, empty exhausted immediately. No mutation/full output allocation; initializing plus m calls costs O(h+m).
templateDetails.observation: Each node pushed/popped once across iterator lifetime.

templateDetails.preconditions: Strict unique-key BST, comparable non-None keys. Returns (largest <= key, smallest >= key), or smallest > key for successor; None means missing. Query key need not exist; no mutation. Min/max follow left/right chains in O(h).
templateDetails.observation: Discarded branches cannot improve saved candidates.

templateDetails.preconditions: Undirected unweighted tree 0..n-1. Validates edge count/cycles/connectivity. Returns sum of edge distances from each vertex; n=0 -> []. No input mutation, consumes edge iterable. Moving root into child shortens size[child] distances and lengthens all others.
templateDetails.observation: Root move makes child_size distances shorter and others longer.

practiceDetails.insight: Depth flows down; height returns up.
Left spine exposes next inorder key.
Push right before left.
Combine only after both child phases.
Swap links once per node.
Compare corresponding shape and values.
Cross-pair left with right.
Require matching leaf, not internal prefix.
Midpoint yields near-equal child sizes.
Comparison discards impossible subtree.
Attach at empty link and retain returned root.
Queue snapshot isolates one level.
Return height and validity together.
Candidate diameter is left height+right height.
Carry every ancestor bound.
Count sorted yields and stop at k.
Retain unfinished left spine between calls.
Verify keys then find first split.
First shared identity ancestor; values irrelevant.
Copy successor then preserve its right child on unlink.
Inorder pointer closes preorder stack ancestors.
Count prefix-target before insert and undo on exit.
Return one arm, combine two for answer.
Nulls preserve missing-child slots.
Root move changes sum by n-2*child_size.
